Judgment calls: (a) Two semicircular crossover arcs, both verified in the raw bitmap: the Diode 8/16 column bulges right around (389,192) where it meets the long y~192 horizontal, and the Resistor 6 bottom column bulges right around (347,386) where it meets the y~386 BJT-15-base wire. Both are CROSSINGS, so n13 stays separate from n4/n5 and n11/0 stays separate from n10. In both cases the arc still grazes the crossed wire (the drafter drew shallow arcs), but the arc is unmistakably a crossover marker drawn on one wire while the other runs straight through. There are no other wire crossings anywhere in this drawing - every other meeting of wires is a T or an L, and the drafter marks the important ones with a filled dot. (b) The y~192 horizontal has an 8 px pen-lift gap between x=396 and x=403 (nothing at all is drawn in it, and both stubs sit at the same y). Read as one wire: the alternative leaves Resistor 7's right terminal on a net with no second terminal. (c) BJT terminal roles were read from the arrow, which is always on the emitter: PNPs 0, 2, 3 and 18 all carry the arrow on their upper lead pointing INTO the base, so for each of them the upper lead is the emitter and the lower lead the collector. NPNs 10, 11, 15, 17 and 21 carry the arrow on their lower lead pointing AWAY from the base, so lower = emitter. This is consistent with the layout in every case (PNP emitters sit on the +3/+5/+6/+10 V nodes, NPN emitters sit on the ground rail). (d) BJT-NPN 11 is drawn mirrored - its base bar is at x~196 with the base lead running RIGHT and both channel leads running left - but the arrow reading is unchanged. (e) Diodes 8 and 16 both point downward (triangle above, cathode bar below), so index 0 = anode = top lead, index 1 = cathode = bottom lead for both. (f) The four supply symbols (V-DC (one port) 4, 12, 19, 20) are single-terminal arrows labelled +6V, +10V, +3V and +5V; each is given the one net its lead touches. They are NOT ground, so none of them is named 0. (g) No component is off-frame: all 22 bbox centres lie inside 512x512 and every symbol is visible in the image. Nothing was added, removed or re-classed; no terminal is left unconnected. (h) Several 1-2 px binarisation dropouts inside resistor zigzags and along the ground rail (e.g. x=340 on the rail, x=250 on the y~194 run, x=322 on the y~279 run) were read as continuous - each sits mid-run on a straight stroke with ink on both sides. (2) The y~192 pen-lift is exactly x=396..402 (7 px, both stubs on row 192); reading it as one wire is what puts Resistor 7's right terminal on n5, and n5's junction dot at (445,190) is a clear local bulge (rows 189-191 span x442-453) that also catches V-DC(one port) 20's dashed lead. (3) The Resistor-14-to-n4 run has a 1-column dropout at x=250 bridged on row 195, the n8 column has a 1-px jog gap at (183,331), the n11 run a 1-column gap at x=322, and the top rail 1-column diagonal steps at x=312 and x=392 - all continuous. Terminals are written (collector, base, emitter) throughout.
